titleEn: Why a company donating $20,000 a month counts for more than $240,000 once a year in the eyes of customers
titleZh: 为何顾客觉得每月捐两万美元，比每年一次捐二十四万美元更慷慨？
method: Machine reference translation with paragraph alignment; not manually certified.

paragraphs.en: People tend to think more highly of companies that give to charity on a monthly or weekly basis rather than donating an annual lump sum worth the same amount.
paragraphs.zh: 人们倾向于更高地评价那些每月或每周向慈善机构捐款的公司，而不是每年一次性捐赠同等金额的公司。

paragraphs.en: This is what I and five other marketing researchers found when we conducted seven studies involving more than 150,000 people. The Journal of Marketing Research, which is peer-reviewed, published our article on the results in early 2026. My co-author Alexander B. Park and I led the team.
paragraphs.zh: 这是我和其他五名营销研究人员在进行了七项涉及15万多人的研究后发现的。同行评议的《营销研究杂志》（Journal of Marketing Research）于2026年初发表了我们关于研究结果的文章。我和我的合著者亚历山大（Alexander B. Park）领导了这个团队。

paragraphs.en: Our goal was to discover whether the way a company communicates with the public about its donations affects how much credit it gets from consumers for those gifts.
paragraphs.zh: 我们的目标是发现一家公司与公众沟通其捐赠的方式是否会影响它从消费者那里获得多少信用。

paragraphs.en: Across seven studies, we found that companies earn more goodwill when they give consistently – say, US$20,000 a month – instead of making a single $240,000 gift. On average, consumers also said they were more likely to buy from those companies.
paragraphs.zh: 通过七项研究，我们发现，如果公司持续捐赠--比如每月2万美元--而不是一次性捐赠24万美元，他们会获得更多的商誉。平均而言，消费者也表示，他们更有可能从这些公司购买产品。

paragraphs.en: To test this premise, we did two real-world studies. First, we partnered with GiftAMeal, a U.S. company that runs a free app for diners. Each time someone takes a photo of their meal at a participating restaurant and shares it on social media, GiftAMeal donates to a local food bank.
paragraphs.zh: 为了验证这一假设，我们做了两个真实世界的研究。首先，我们与GiftAMeal合作，这是一家为食客提供免费应用程序的美国公司。每当有人在参与活动的餐厅拍下用餐照片并分享到社交媒体上时，GiftAMeal就会向当地的食品银行捐款。

paragraphs.en: We ran two versions of GiftAMeal’s Facebook ad, which together reached 67,576 people. One said the company “donated 25,000 meals every month” last year. The other said it “donated 300,000 meals” last year. Both were true, and everything else about the ads was the same. We found that people who saw the monthly version were about 21% more likely to click on the ad.
paragraphs.zh: 我们对GiftAMeal的Facebook广告做了两个版本的测试，总共有67,576人观看。一个版本说该公司去年“每月捐赠25,000份餐”。另一个版本说该公司去年“捐赠300,000份餐”。两个版本都是真的，广告的其他内容也是一样的。我们发现，看了每月版本的人点击广告的可能性要高出21%。

paragraphs.en: Next, we worked with Salt + Smoke, a Midwestern barbecue restaurant. When we emailed 75,514 customers who subscribed to its newsletters, half read that the company would give $5,000 a month from September through December to a small, local charity that supports early childhood education programs. The other half read that it would make a one-time donation of $20,000.
paragraphs.zh: 接下来，我们与美国中西部的一家烧烤餐厅Salt + Smoke合作。当我们给订阅了该公司通讯的75,514名顾客发送电子邮件时，其中一半人读到，该公司将从9月到12月每月向当地一家支持儿童早期教育项目的小型慈善机构捐赠5,000美元。另一半人读到，该公司将一次性捐赠2万美元。

paragraphs.en: Subscribers who read about the monthly donation pledge were nearly twice as likely to click through to the restaurant’s website as those who read about the one-time gift pledge even though the total was the same.
paragraphs.zh: 阅读每月捐赠承诺的订阅者点击餐厅网站的可能性几乎是阅读一次性捐赠承诺的订阅者的两倍，尽管总数相同。

paragraphs.en: Then we ran online experiments with more than 7,400 people to learn why and when consistent giving makes people view a company more favorably. We found that, on average, when a company gives monthly, people see its charitable support as a more genuine commitment to the causes.
paragraphs.zh: 然后，我们对7,400多人进行了在线实验，以了解为什么以及何时持续的捐赠会让人们对一家公司产生更好的看法。我们发现，平均而言，当一家公司每月捐赠一次时，人们会将其慈善支持视为对事业的更真诚的承诺。

paragraphs.en: Why it matters
paragraphs.zh: Why it matters

paragraphs.en: U.S. companies gave nearly $44 billion in 2025 alone. And this kind of giving is popular with the public. In a 2022 survey, 88% of Americans said it’s important for companies to make the world a better place.
paragraphs.zh: 仅在2025年，美国公司就捐赠了近440亿美元。这种捐赠受到公众的欢迎。在2022年的一项调查中，88%的美国人表示，公司让世界变得更美好很重要。

paragraphs.en: Companies frequently promote their donations with the largest numbers they can muster. For example, Microsoft announced that the software giant and its employees donated $256 million in 2025; Walmart and its foundation say they have donated $2 billion in 2026.
paragraphs.zh: 公司经常用他们能收集到的最大数字来宣传他们的捐赠。例如，微软宣布，这家软件巨头及其员工在2025年捐赠了2.56亿美元;沃尔玛及其基金会表示，他们在2026年捐赠了20亿美元。

paragraphs.en: Yet boasting about big numbers may not impress people as much as emphasizing the consistency of donations. This may help explain why companies often struggle to convey their charitable efforts in ways that win people over.
paragraphs.zh: 然而，吹嘘巨额捐款并不像强调捐款的一致性那样能给人们留下深刻印象。这或许有助于解释为什么企业往往难以用赢得人心的方式来传达自己的慈善努力。

paragraphs.en: Even if companies give only once a year, they can indicate that they are engaged in a steady pattern of giving. For example, they can make their annual gifts on Giving Tuesday every year. Donating on the same day or as part of the same fundraising campaign every year can signal an ongoing commitment, not a one-off.
paragraphs.zh: 即使公司一年只捐赠一次，他们也可以表明他们正在进行一种稳定的捐赠模式。例如，他们可以在每年的“捐赠星期二”进行年度捐赠。在同一天捐赠或每年作为同一筹款活动的一部分捐赠可以表明持续的承诺，而不是一次性的。

paragraphs.en: What still isn’t known
paragraphs.zh: 我们还不知道的是

paragraphs.en: We don’t yet know how long the reputational boost companies may get from recurring donations might last, or whether those donations can translate into long-term customer loyalty.
paragraphs.zh: 我们还不知道公司从经常性捐赠中获得的声誉提升能持续多久，也不知道这些捐赠是否能转化为长期的客户忠诚度。

paragraphs.en: It’s also possible that what we found would not apply during emergencies. For example, consumers might be happy to see a company make one big gift right after a hurricane when a local community’s needs are immense.
paragraphs.zh: 我们的发现也有可能不适用于紧急情况。例如，当当地社区的需求巨大时，消费者可能很高兴看到一家公司在飓风过后立即制作一份大礼。

paragraphs.en: What’s next
paragraphs.zh: 下一步是什么

paragraphs.en: Along with Park and Cynthia Cryder, a Washington University in St. Louis marketing professor, I’m now studying other ways that corporate philanthropy can affect how much credit companies get for doing good. So far, we’ve found that companies may earn less goodwill when they ask customers to chip in to their charitable campaigns. People seem to expect companies to carry more of the load themselves.
paragraphs.zh: 沿着帕克和华盛顿大学圣路易斯分校（University in St. Louis）营销学教授辛西娅·克莱德（Cynthia Cryder），我正在研究企业慈善行为影响企业因行善而获得多少信用的其他方式。到目前为止，我们发现，当企业要求客户为慈善活动捐款时，它们获得的善意可能会减少。人们似乎希望企业自己承担更多的负担。

paragraphs.en: The Research Brief is a short take about interesting academic work.
paragraphs.zh: 研究简报是关于有趣的学术工作的简短介绍。
